# Mago walks into a agriculture, food & harvest firm

Somewhere right now, in a agriculture, food & harvest office, someone is doing exactly what the myths describe — and has never heard of **Mago**. This file is the introduction.

## Before the Office, the Story

**Mago Shapes the Land.** In Korean folktales, Mago Halmi is so enormous that her body becomes the landscape.  Her urine forms rivers, her sighs become wind, and her skirt covers mountains.  She creates the topography of Korea through her movements and labour.

**The Skirt That Covered Mountains.** A widespread motif tells how Mago spread her skirt to cover or move mountains, creating valleys and peaks.  The motif links female creative power to textile work and to the shaping of the earth.

## Not the First Rebrand

Mago sits at the intersection of Korean shamanism, Chinese Daoist folklore, and contemporary goddess spirituality.  Chinese sources know Magu as an immortal associated with hemp and longevity; Korean sources transform her into a creator grandmother. The office is only the latest translation.
